name: Britannia Industries Ltd
title: Britannia Industries Ltd - 500825 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue up 9.5% with volume near 9% and June exit in mid-teens after dual-pricing disruption ended; but LPG, palm oil and sugar inflation only half offset by price, so margin defence is uncertain.

triggers.label: Price offset only half of inflation
triggers.quote: at best, we have been able to mitigate half of the inflation through price increases. The other half, we have not been able to.

triggers.label: Exit quarter mid-teens growth
triggers.quote: we actually exited the quarter in double digits kind of mid-teens number

triggers.label: Growth not from channel stocking
triggers.quote: We don't see any of this as a result of any inventory buildup. It is a result of demand buildup

triggers.label: Further 1.5-2% pricing to come
triggers.quote: you will probably see maybe another 1.5% to 2% coming in

guidance.value: No numeric guidance; margins to be managed between value, volume and margin
guidance.quote: we will have to manage between value, volume and margin and which we will do

red_flags.label: Input cost inflation (LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar)
red_flags.quote: the reality is that it is there to stay, and we have to use that to manufacture

red_flags.label: International business disruption
red_flags.quote: we have seen 4 months of turbulence and there were challenges

evasions.quote: I wouldn't want to give a number in terms of percentage of what we are doing.

evasions.topic: Full-year good year definition / margin outlook
evasions.quote: Whether this holds good for the rest of the year, we will have to see.

summary.headline: Britannia Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9.5% to INR 4,964 crore, with ~9% tonnage volume growth and PAT margin at 11.9%.
summary.overview: Management said revenue from operations on a consolidated basis was about INR 4,964 crore, up 9.5% YoY, with standalone growth at 10%. PAT was 11.9% of revenue and grew 13.6% YoY. Management said the quarter exited in mid-teens growth after dual-pricing disruption in rural and wholesale channels faded in June. Input cost inflation from LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk is a headwind, and management said only about half of it has been offset through price increases so far.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 52 crore last year, as stated by an analyst
none booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: Management said GT demand picked up, with the recent run-rate about 1.5x the full-year FY26 growth rate. Key states are growing and other states are growing about 1.3x faster.

segments.name: E-commerce / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce grew at strong double digits. Quick commerce is about 80-85% of e-commerce and is growing at healthy double digits.

segments.name: Other channels
segments.commentary: Newer channels were growing at about 2.5x the GT rate overall.

segments.name: Dairy and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Dairy grew at double digits. Cake, rusk and wafers grew at double digits led by portfolio innovation. Croissant lines were growing above 30% and Croissant run-rate was about INR 200 crore annualised (INR 100 crore ARR doubled).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mixed quarter: pressure in Middle East and Saudi Arabia and headwinds in North America, offset by growth in Africa led by Kenya. Management expects a return to growth from this quarter.

segments.name: Eastern India
segments.commentary: Growing in double digits per management.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give explicit FY27 guidance. It said the team is confident of a good year, defined as balanced growth across volume, value and profitability.
Management expects roughly 1.5-2% more price realisation from shrinkflation changes to come through in the coming quarters, after about 1% in Q1.
Management said it is watching sugar, palm oil, milk and LPG/PNG costs ahead of the festive season and said the current cost level is higher than in February 2026.
Management said Q2 faces a base effect in September from the GST price transition last year, and July and August were normal months.
Brand-building spend is running ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given.
capex_capacity: Management said it is working to reduce LPG/PNG dependence through biomass and alternate fuels, but no timelines were given.
Renewable energy share in plant power rose 16%, and management is working to expand it under state rules.
A new Chief Business Officer for Dairy was appointed and a Strategy and Corporate Development head joined, with management saying the leadership team is now complete.
demand_pricing: Q1 volume growth was about 9% in tonnage terms; pricing contributed about 1% and was mainly shrinkflation in INR 5 and INR 10 packs.
Management said dual pricing disruption in rural and wholesale was felt in April and early May and ended in June. Demand was described as holding up.
Industrial fuel inflation was steep: LPG and PNG roughly 2.5x in April-May, now about 1.5x February levels. Palm oil is near INR 140 per kg, up more than 20%.
Management said it could mitigate about half of input inflation through price increases so far.
Sugar rose more than INR 7 per kg in the last 2-3 weeks. Flour has held up, but El Nino and rainfall are a watch item for wheat prices.
Management said it has regained market share on a sequential basis across many biscuit categories, following the end of dual pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the mid-teens exit growth in June, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company sells in based on sell-out, so no loading. The dual-pricing impact ended in June, which brought back some buyers, and organic demand held up. It gave no forward indication.

qa_highlights.question: How will ad spend and input inflation affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LPG prices are about 1.5x February levels and sugar and palm oil are also up. Brand spend is ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given. Management said half of inflation has been offset by price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA margin hold at or above FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the input cost base is higher than in February. It did not commit to full-year margins, but said it is confident of managing levers across value, volume and margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there PLI benefits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no PLI incentive was booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27, because the threshold growth was not achieved.

qa_highlights.question: How is Britannia responding to GT competition in Eastern India and other areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited regional empowerment, targeted media and influencer spend, and local product innovation such as Milk Bikis Thirukkural packs in Tamil Nadu. Sub-distributors are being converted to direct distributors.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the GST impact on volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said over 60% of sales are at INR 5 and INR 10 price points, so GST-cut elasticity will be gradual and smaller than for higher-priced packs.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk, with festive-season sugar pressure and monsoon/El Nino risk to wheat and flour.
Margin pressure from higher brand spend and only partial pass-through of input costs (about half so far).
International business: Middle East, Saudi Arabia and North America remain weak, and geopolitical developments are uncertain.
Whether the mid-teens exit growth and 9% volume growth can be sustained after dual-pricing normalisation.
Competitive intensity in GT, plus a September GST base effect in Q2.
Health and regulatory shift toward healthy snacking; management is building a health and protein platform, with no timelines given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the GT recovery, but cautious on input costs and margins. Management gave no numerical FY27 margin or volume guidance and declined to forecast beyond Q1.
key_quotes: So we have exited the quarter on a very positive note.
At best, we have been able to mitigate half of the inflation through price increases.
So you should not hold it on to the P&L like a permanent phenomenon.
So the wholesale channel and the rural channel, where the dual pricing had an impact is now over, and we see that the throughput, both in terms of selling in and selling out is very good.

growth.why: No explicit FY27 numeric guidance; management expects roughly 1.5-2% more price realisation from shrinkflation and says it is confident of a balanced good year, with growth backed mainly by ~9% volume and exit-rate mid-teens, but no capacity or order book cited.
